title: The Rydberg sensitivity-bandwidth trade-off has never been measured; the published 'frontier' is a hull-construction artifact

result.central negative result: There is no empirical sensitivity-bandwidth frontier in the published record. The four papers defining the SENSITIVITY axis (Sedlacek 2012, Jing 2020, Sci. Adv. 2024, Commun. Phys. 2026) state NO instantaneous bandwidth at all; every paper stating an IBW comes from the bandwidth-engineering literature. The trade-off is constructed by placing one lab's sensitivity beside another lab's bandwidth.
result.correlation on the 8 papers that state b: alpha = -0.14 +/- 0.53, R^2 = 0.012 (OLS, log-log). Zero correlation; even the SIGN is undetermined. Defensible convention/inclusion choices move alpha over -0.28..+0.74, with R^2 never above 0.38.
result.the folklore alpha ~ 1 is a statistical: The clean Pareto hull (alpha = 0.67 +/- 0.11, R^2 = 0.95) is produced by hull construction, not by physics. A Monte-Carlo null with NO trade, matched to the observed marginals, yields hulls with median alpha = 1.27 and median R^2 = 0.85; P(hull alpha >= 0.669) = 0.80. A constant NEF x IBW product is precisely what uncorrelated points look like once a hull is drawn around them. The actual published product spans 81x.
result.comparability exceeds the signal: At matched bandwidth (~9-21 MHz) published NEF spans 31x (62 nV/cm/rtHz ECNU vs 1910 nV/cm/rtHz NIST) — larger than the entire dynamic range of the claimed frontier.
result.the definitions do not agree: Three mutually incompatible IBW definitions are in use, spanning 3.46x. NIST's is internally inconsistent: it equates a factor of 2 in FIELD with a 3 dB drop, but a factor of 2 in field is 6 dB.
result.two primary sources falsify the folklore: Manchaiah et al. (NIST, arXiv:2509.20632): 'we demonstrate that sensitivity is preserved while achieving a response bandwidth of 8 MHz', with the preceding sentence naming the belief as folklore. And arXiv:2607.25309 improves on the same group's prior result on BOTH axes (147 nV/cm/rtHz at >100 MHz vs 222.6 at 76.8 MHz).
result.relation to this program's simulation: RydSim's corrected engine predicts a WEAK trade above an interior optimum (alpha ~ 0.18, 3.55x bandwidth for 1.26x sensitivity). The literature does not contradict this — it contains no measurement capable of contradicting it.
result.the decisive experiment already has data: Manchaiah et al. Fig. 4 reports NEF vs beat frequency at five coupling powers (20/60/100/140/160 mW) on ONE apparatus, but extracts no IBW per curve and fits no exponent. Re-analysing that single published figure would produce the field's first real trade exponent.

config.method: 24-agent web-verified literature audit; every load-bearing claim passed to an independent skeptic instructed to refute it
config.areas: empirical frontier, fundamental bounds, mechanism, claim audit
config.corpus: 8 papers stating both axes; 14 data points extracted

uncertainty_budget.no published error bars: Not one of the eight (NEF, IBW) pairs carries a stated uncertainty on either coordinate. All fits assume equal weights and no errors-in-variables; quoted alpha uncertainties are LOWER BOUNDS.
uncertainty_budget.convention unrecoverable: Amplitude vs RMS is stated by nobody in the set. Pinned for Sci. Adv. 2024 only, via spec 08's antenna cross-check (T_eq 828 K computed vs 830 K published).
uncertainty_budget.figure digitisation: Several points are INFERRED from figures rather than stated; each is tagged as such in the underlying report.

caveats: This is a NEGATIVE result about the literature, not a positive measurement of the trade. It establishes that the folklore is unsupported, NOT that no trade exists.

Band-averaged sensitivity is reported by nobody: every published pair is (best-case NEF at the optimal beat frequency, full-span IBW). In-band variation reaches 5.44x in one case, so published pairs systematically understate the trade by an unknown factor of order 1-5.

No IBW exists for ANY high-sensitivity result. For Sci. Adv. 2024 the within-shot atomic response bandwidth is unmeasured; if it is MHz-class (plausible for cold atoms: no Doppler, no transit) that paper becomes a high-sensitivity HIGH-bandwidth point and the narrative inverts.

Whether the engineering knobs (transit time, beam radius, Omega_c, Omega_p, Doppler geometry, dephasing) can be varied INDEPENDENTLY at fixed atom number and optical depth is unestablished. A constraint collapsing them onto one manifold is the only candidate for a fundamental trade, and nobody has published it. That is exactly what RydSim is positioned to test.
validation_state: literature audit; every load-bearing claim adversarially refuted by an independent agent before inclusion
